Good afternoon. My name is Sean Erkin. I am here today to present the annual Zoning By-law update.
Every year, the City staff prepare minor technical and administrative amendments to the Zoning By-law
to improve clarity and consistency and provide flexibility while maintaining the intent of the
Zoning By-laws. These improvements are identified through consultation and working files with
builders and developers, experience of planning and zoning staff, alignment with other departments,
primarily emergency services, transportation and engineering,
alignment with provincial legislation and regional standards, and general inquiries.
These proposed changes are further refined through consultation with staff, builders,
and developers. The complete list of changes are outlined in Appendix C, the rationale chart.
I would like to take a few moments to highlight some of the key changes proposed.
Starting with unobstructed walkways, these are required for additional dwelling units
and multiple dwellings with 10 units and fewer. The current requirements are spread out through
the general regulations and within the actual definition of the unstructured walkway itself.
The proposed amendments seek to create a centralized location for consistency and ease of
reference and then adding new regulations for maximum slope, cross-slope and length for safe
and suitable access so that emergency services can access the dwelling unit in the event of an
emergency. It is important to note that we are proposing amendments to steps and access
ramps that would create increased flexibility for this unstructured walkway by allowing
different types of steps to be located within the side yard while maintaining the intent
for drainage. Private home daycares. Currently, right now, the city and region are experiencing
a significant shortage of daycare space, with waitlists often spanning multiple years. Private
private home daycares are part of the solution towards this to provide a flexible and economic
option for parents.
Private home daycares are regulated by the province with help from regional consultants
through the Child Care and Early Years Act of 2014.
This regulation provides thorough inspection and complaint investigation process with every
single complaint being followed up.
They also provide regulations such as the maximum number of children versus licensed
or unlicensed and when you have to count your own children within those numbers.
The proposed amendments seek to allow private home day care in any dwelling unit for increased
flexibility while also removing current limitations that are considered inconsistent or incompatible
with standard practices and provincial legislation.
For example, removing the limit of a maximum of 25% of the dwelling unit used for private
home daycare when children are generally free to play or nap throughout the dwelling unit.
The proposed amendments seek to introduce a new option for bicycle lockers, which will be for
the Class A or Class C bicycle lockers that will allow an increased flexibility and potential space
efficiency. This is a wedge-shaped or pie-shaped, as shown on the screen. These were developed by
the transportation department and consider the minimum size necessary to accommodate approximately
85% of all bikes. The proposed amendments also introduce exceptions to allow a reduced minimum
block width for townhouses and multiple dwellings for increased flexibility while maintaining the
intent of the zoning bylay. This allows a 5-metre block width for townhouses rather than 5.5 or 6
depending on the zone. This maintains the intent of consistent streetscapes and proportions of
driveways to the actual dwelling itself. We are proposing to allow a minimum of 14-metre
log width for multiple dwellings with 10 units or fewer in the RES 5 zone for increased flexibility.
This would allow suitable space for an appropriately sized building while still
adhering to minimum landscaping, amenity space, setbacks and enough space within a
side yard for a driveway leading to a rear yard parking area.
The proposed amendments also seek to introduce a new general regulation and overlay to help
with the consistent application and ease of reference of recent provincial legislation.
Changes of the planning act and inventory regulation allow certain properties to benefit
from a 98% compliance with required setbacks.
This regulation clearly specifies where they are permitted and not permitted for this reduction
and setbacks for ease of reference. It is important to note that this change to the
Planning Act and Ontario regulations are already in effect.
Staff also note that there was one change related to the regulation, setbacks to lot lines with
common walls for townhouses. That was outlined in Appendix C to the report that was initially
missed in the amending by-law to 2019-051 in front of the committee tonight. Based on
our committee's direction, staff would support updating the proposed 2019 051 bylaw to include
the language that is shown in Appendix C. In conclusion, staff are satisfied that the
proposed zoning bylaw amendment is consistent with the provincial planning statement, complies
with Kitchener's Official Plan, the Region of Waterloo Official Plan and applicable legislation
and represents good planning principles. Staff recommend approval of the proposed amendments.
